notes: Round 10 runs several tracks at once, each in its own worktree: M1 (land animals), M2 (water mobs), M3 (night mobs) and W's w3 (the game events W's first merge left out). D0's d0b (silverfish in stone, endermites from pearls, flying navigation) is merged (c0366f3a), and release 6 is built with PROTOCOL 11 (789f6d23). Never bump minecraft_net::PROTOCOL: the release step bumps it once when messages changed; if a commit changes a ToClient/ToServer message or the codec, add a line under '## Protocol' in the track log. Insert new match arms and list entries next to related ones, not at the end of lists, to keep merges small (E3-0 names the few positional lists that are appended). Record decisions in the track log. LOAD: builds run at -j 4 per slot to keep the laptop cool; never start a second cargo command, the game, or any other long CPU-heavy process. Keep to the brief: each section names the commit its file:line anchors come from, so re-check every anchor before editing; keep off the hooks the M briefs own and follow the cross-area overlaps (both in E3-0). E2's e2b (44d96765) and D0's d0b (c0366f3a) are merged, so every 'waits for e2b', 'after d0b' and 'release 6 built' in the brief is met; d0b moved lines in server.rs, world.rs, walk_path.rs, entity_view.rs and families.rs, so anchors taken before it need a re-check. The orchestrator brings track-e3 up to minecraft-survival before each segment, so the review uses git diff r10-e3t-base..HEAD as usual. SEGMENT e3t: E3-14: ominous shots, the shared clock and crouching players, vault looks, lodestones in unloaded chunks, and thrown things saved. WAITS: W's w3 merged. D0's d0b is merged (c0366f3a).

Track E3 group trial-clock: build track-e3.md section E3-14 group trial-clock. Commits: 1. Minecraft levels take the world's game time back when a player returns. 2. Minecraft trial spawners see a crouching player's eyes and drop items above their head. Key points: (1) minecraft_survival server.rs close_empty_levels: an occupied level whose empty_ticks > 0 gets entities.set_game_time(globals.game_time()) for every dimension, beside the weather resync; test it next to the_overworld_takes_the_world_s_weather_back_when_a_player_returns, and add the no-save variant. (2) TrialPlayer.height; standing 1.8/1.62 and crouching 1.5/1.27 (Avatar.POSES) replace PLAYER_HEIGHT; tick_trial_spawners takes &input.controls (sneaking, which also covers MW2 prone) for the height and the eyes used for sight (PlayerDetector uses getEyePosition); item_spot uses the height. Do not add fields to PlayerControls (M1 owns the next one); swimming and gliding are left. The owner's steps and the kit line are in the brief.

Track E3 group vault-looks: build track-e3.md section E3-14 group vault-looks. Commits: 1. Minecraft vaults forget the ejection count on load like vanilla. 2. Minecraft stacked items in vaults and on the ground are drawn like vanilla. Key points: (1) vault.rs Vaults gains an ejections map beside fail_times; tick_vaults and insert_key take total_ejections_needed from it (missing means 0) right after Vault::read and before before is cloned, then store the new total back; tick_vaults drops entries of vaults it no longer lists. Vanilla VaultServerData.set skips totalEjectionsNeeded, so after a load the pitch starts at 0.8 + 0.4 x items left and falls. (2) vault_display::cluster_offsets follows ItemEntityRenderer.renderMultipleFromCount: flat models (bounding box z size after the ground transform at most 0.0625) stack copies 1.5 x zsize apart in z, centred, with x and y jitter of +-0.075 after the first; other models jitter +-0.15 on all three axes; seed from the item's raw id plus damage when reachable, else a stable hash without the count (log which). ItemVisual gains depth; vault items and dropped item copies (mesh.rs:1042-1065) both use the helper. The owner's steps and the kit line are in the brief.

Track E3 group lodestones-unloaded: build track-e3.md section E3-14 group lodestones-unloaded. Commit: Minecraft lodestone compasses check lodestones in unloaded chunks. Key points: ServerSim.saved_lodestones (ChunkPos to Vec<BlockPos>). Add a lodestones_in(chunk) scan with the POI table, as load_pois does. unload_chunk records the level chunk's lodestones before remove_chunk (empty lists too); load_chunk removes the entry. lodestones_gone becomes &mut self: a loaded chunk checks the block; an unloaded one uses the entry or reads the saved chunk once through storage.load, caching the result (no saved chunk or no storage means no lodestone, as vanilla PoiManager.existsAtPosition has no record there). Update a_broken_lodestone_is_reported_only_when_its_chunk_is_loaded: its never-loaded far target is now gone; rename it. Add the unload and region-file tests. The owner's steps (the fork's /give takes no lodestone_tracker component, so step 1 locks a compass, leaves it in a chest 1500 blocks away, breaks the lodestone and takes the compass back: it spins; a locked compass 1500 blocks away still points, also after a reload) and the kit line are in the brief.

Track E3 group thrown-saved: build track-e3.md section E3-14 group thrown-saved. Commit: Minecraft snowballs, eggs, potions, bottles and wind charges in flight are saved. Key points: thrown::to_tag and thrown::from_tag, next to Thrown::resumed, write and read vanilla's ThrowableItemProjectile fields: the entity id by kind; Item through item_nbt with its components; Pos, Motion, Rotation, Owner, LeftOwner and HasBeenShot. A player's wind charge has no Item but has acceleration_power, like the breeze charge. Ender pearls give None and stay unsaved (vanilla keeps them in the player file: left for later). breeze_charge keeps its id and calls the shared writer and reader. server.rs save_chunk_entities saves through thrown::to_tag with the owner's UUID (mob shooter or player); unload keeps only pearls; add_saved_entity loads through thrown::from_tag. tick_thrown gives a resumed thing back to an online player whose UUID matches, as tridents do (Thrown::set_player_owner also sets the flight's owner id). D0's d0b (tick_thrown) is merged. The owner's steps (throw, then Save and Quit at once, then load) and the kit line are in the brief.
